Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Tight chest for 3 hours, associated with mild shortness of breath.
- Symptom history: Mild wheeze and cough (persistent, non-productive), cough worse at night but also present during the day. Recent cold last week (runny nose, sore throat, currently improved). Reports feeling generally under the weather.
- Denies chest pain.
- Breathlessness present when walking up stairs, not at rest (except for sensation of chest tightness).
- Past medical history: Asthma (childhood hospital admission with intubation at age 16–17 for severe exacerbation), hayfever, childhood eczema, childhood milk protein allergy, dust allergy.
- Family history: Mother has eczema, father has asthma.
- Medications: Ventolin (Salbutamol) inhaler (dose/route/frequency not documented); Clenil Modulite (inhaled steroid) (dose/route/frequency not documented). Has not used either for approximately 1 week due to running out and not refilling prescriptions.
- Allergies: No known drug allergies; allergic to dust (not drug-related).
- Social history: No details documented.

Objective:
- No shortness of breath at rest (except for reported chest tightness).
- Shortness of breath noted with exertion (climbing stairs).
- No physical examination documented.
- No vitals or investigations performed or documented.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Asthma Exacerbation:
   - Assessment: Likely mild to moderate asthma exacerbation, triggered by recent upper respiratory tract infection and non-adherence to maintenance inhalers.
   - Differential diagnosis: Upper respiratory tract infection residual effects.
   - Investigations planned: None in transcript.
   - Treatment planned:
     - Prescribe Salbutamol (Ventolin) inhaler (dose/route/frequency not documented).
     - Prescribe Clenil Modulite inhaler (dose/route/frequency not documented).
     - Short course of oral steroids (5 days; specific medication, dose, and route not documented—plan: 2 tablets in the morning for 5 days).
     - Prescribe a spacer device with instructions for use.
     - Advise to rest and consider time off work, self-certify if off work for up to 7 days.
   - Safety-netting advice:
     - Seek medical attention if using Ventolin more frequently than every 3 hours, worsening symptoms (increased shortness of breath, chest pain/tightness, light-headedness), or any other concerns.
